name: Incident Handling & Coordination
description: Ability to lead and coordinate the handling of security incidents across their full lifecycle, following the CSF 2.0-aligned model of NIST SP 800-61r3 and the phases of ISO/IEC 27035. Covers incident declaration and classification, severity and priority assignment, incident command roles, evidence-aware decision making, stakeholder, customer, and regulator notification (including statutory deadlines such as GDPR, NIS2, and DORA), communication cadence and status reporting, and post-incident lessons-learned reviews. Hands-on collection belongs to DFIR-IR-LIVE and containment actions to DFIR-IR-CONTAIN.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to incident handling or coordination

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the incident response lifecycle and the roles involved in handling an incident
evidence: Can describe the CSF 2.0-aligned incident response model of NIST SP 800-61r3 and the ISO/IEC 27035 incident management phases
Can distinguish a security event from a declared incident and explain why declaration matters
Can name the typical incident roles (incident commander, scribe, technical lead, communications lead, legal)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Supports incident handling under the direction of an incident lead
evidence: Maintained an incident log and decision record during a live incident or tabletop under supervision
Drafted internal status updates and stakeholder briefings reviewed by the incident lead
Applied the lab severity matrix to classify incidents with supervisor confirmation
Tracked evidence, actions, and owners in the incident tracking system

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently leads incidents of moderate scope from declaration to closure
evidence: Led 5+ incidents as incident commander through declaration, response, and closure
Determined notification obligations (contractual, GDPR Art. 33, NIS2, DORA or sectoral) and met the applicable deadlines
Ran a defined communications cadence with technical teams, management, and external parties
Facilitated post-incident reviews producing tracked corrective actions

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Coordinates complex, multi-party or high-severity incidents and mentors incident leads
evidence: Coordinated incidents involving multiple organisations, third-party providers, law enforcement, or insurers
Balanced business continuity, evidence preservation, and legal privilege in escalation decisions
Designed and ran tabletop exercises that exposed and closed gaps in the response plan
Reviews incident records and lessons-learned reports of other incident leads

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's incident management capability and is a recognised authority on incident handling
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's incident response plan, playbooks, and severity model
Aligned the incident management process with ISO/IEC 27035 and regulatory reporting regimes
Advises executive leadership and boards during crisis-level incidents
Published or presented on incident management practice

assessment_methods.description: Lead a facilitated tabletop exercise for a ransomware or data-breach scenario, including declaration, severity assignment, notification decisions with deadlines, and a stakeholder briefing
Review incident logs, decision records, notifications, and lessons-learned reports from recent incidents for completeness, timeliness, and traceability
